sections.kicker: Made for the way you work
sections.title: One less thing between you and bed.
sections.lede: Set up the end of the night while you are still at your desk.

items.title: Choose your ending
items.body: Pick a duration or a clock time, then choose shutdown, sleep, restart, hibernate or log out.

items.title: Keep the controls close
items.body: Use the desktop or paired Android companion to pause, snooze or cancel the session.

items.title: Change your mind
items.body: A grace period and emergency cancel keep you in control. Try Dry Run to rehearse without a power action.

items.title: Make it a ritual
items.body: Start with a Night Mode or save a profile for the routine you use most — and let First Light schedule the morning, with proof of every run.

items.title: Why is Windows warning me when I run this?
items.body: Because this build is not code-signed, Windows may show an unrecognized-app or "Windows protected your PC" warning, depending on Windows security and reputation checks. Verify the published SHA-256 before deciding whether to run it.

items.title: Is this signed?
items.body: No. The installer EXE and the portable ZIP are both unsigned Windows builds — not Authenticode code-signed. Code signing is a separate, tracked piece of future work, not something this release claims.

items.title: What does "Reality Gate Verified" mean?
items.body: It means this exact build passed a full, real, 20-step automated validation pipeline — including packaged-app checks and live physical-phone companion automation — and produced a cryptographically signed, independently verified proof receipt. It does not mean the file is digitally signed, and it has no effect on Windows SmartScreen.

items.title: Is this hosted on GitHub?
items.body: A GitHub release record exists for accountability, but anonymous downloads are blocked there. Canonical public downloads are served from the Proof Foundry download mirror by design.

items.title: How do I verify the download?
items.body: Run the Get-FileHash command in the Release status & evidence section below and compare the result to the published SHA-256. If they don't match exactly, don't run the file.

items.title: Is the Android app also {{product.versionLabel}}?
items.body: The public Android companion remains at {{product.companionPublicVersionLabel}}. A companion v{{product.companionVersion}} build exists alongside Windows {{product.versionLabel}} but has not been released publicly. The current public versions are Windows {{product.versionLabel}} and Android companion {{product.companionPublicVersionLabel}}.
